problem:
Consider the following inhomogeneous system of linear differential equations: $$ {x}^{′}(t)=[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}]x(t)+[\begin{aligned}-3{t}^{2}+4t-4 \\ -{t}^{2}-2t+1\end{aligned}]. $$ The complementary solution to this system is given by $$ {x}_{c}(t)={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{t}+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}t+2 \\ t+1\end{aligned}]{e}^{t},\,{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\in R. $$ Then, the general solution of the system is
$x(t)={x}_{c}(t)+\,\,$ $1$ $\,\,{t}^{2}+\,\,$ {{field-1}} $\,\,t+\,\,$ $1$ .

Recall that the general solution of an inhomogeneous system can be written as 

$$
x(t)={x}_{c}(t)+{x}_{p}(t)
$$

where ${x}_{c}(t)$ is the complementary solution (solution of the corresponding homogeneous system) and ${x}_{p}(t)$ is a particular solution.

The forcing term

$$
[\begin{aligned}-3{t}^{2}+4t-4 \\ -{t}^{2}-2t+1\end{aligned}]
$$

of the inhomogeneous system of ODEs is polynomial of degree $2.$ Therefore, we assume that the particular solution is also polynomial of degree $2,$ i.e.

$$
{x}_{p}(t)=[\begin{aligned}{a}_{1}{t}^{2}+{b}_{1}t+{c}_{1} \\ {a}_{2}{t}^{2}+{b}_{2}t+{c}_{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}{a}_{1} \\ {a}_{2}\end{aligned}]{t}^{2}+[\begin{aligned}{b}_{1} \\ {b}_{2}\end{aligned}]t+[\begin{aligned}{c}_{1} \\ {c}_{2}\end{aligned}],
$$

where ${a}_{1},{a}_{2},{b}_{1},{b}_{2},{c}_{1},{c}_{2}$ are constants that are to be determined. 

Calculating the derivative of ${x}_{p}$ with respect to $t$ gives

$$
{x}_{p}^{′}(t)=[\begin{aligned}2{a}_{1}t+{b}_{1} \\ 2{a}_{2}t+{b}_{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2{a}_{1} \\ 2{a}_{2}\end{aligned}]t+[\begin{aligned}{b}_{1} \\ {b}_{2}\end{aligned}].
$$

To find the unknown constants, we substitute ${x}_{p}$ and ${x}_{p}^{′}$ into our system:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}2{a}_{1} \\ 2{a}_{2}\end{aligned}]t+[\begin{aligned}{b}_{1} \\ {b}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}]([\begin{aligned}{a}_{1} \\ {a}_{2}\end{aligned}]{t}^{2}+[\begin{aligned}{b}_{1} \\ {b}_{2}\end{aligned}]t+[\begin{aligned}{c}_{1} \\ {c}_{2}\end{aligned}])+[\begin{aligned}-3{t}^{2}+4t-4 \\ -{t}^{2}-2t+1\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}2{a}_{1}t+{b}_{1} \\ 2{a}_{2}t+{b}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}2({a}_{1}{t}^{2}+{b}_{1}t+{c}_{1})-({a}_{2}{t}^{2}+{b}_{2}t+{c}_{2}) \\ {a}_{1}{t}^{2}+{b}_{1}t+{c}_{1}\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-3{t}^{2}+4t-4 \\ -{t}^{2}-2t+1\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}0{t}^{2}+2{a}_{1}t+{b}_{1} \\ 0{t}^{2}+2{a}_{2}t+{b}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}(2{a}_{1}-{a}_{2}-3){t}^{2}+(2{b}_{1}-{b}_{2}+4)t+(2{c}_{1}-{c}_{2}-4) \\ ({a}_{1}-1){t}^{2}+({b}_{1}-2)t+({c}_{1}+1)\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}2{a}_{1}-{a}_{2}-3=0 \\ 2{b}_{1}-{b}_{2}+4=2{a}_{1} \\ 2{c}_{1}-{c}_{2}-4={b}_{1} \\ {a}_{1}-1=0 \\ {b}_{1}-2=2{a}_{2} \\ {c}_{1}+1={b}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Solving the fourth equation and then substituting the corresponding values ​​into the first and fifth equations to solve for ${a}_{2}$ and ${b}_{2},$ we get 

$$
{a}_{1}=1,\,{a}_{2}=-1,\,{b}_{1}=0.
$$

 

We substitute these into the second equation to solve for ${b}_{2},$ and then into the sixth and third equations to solve for ${c}_{1}$ and ${c}_{2}.$ We finally get

$$
{b}_{2}=2,\,{c}_{1}=-1,\,{c}_{2}=-2.
$$

 

Therefore, the particular solution is

$$
{x}_{p}(t)=[\begin{aligned}{t}^{2}+1 \\ -\,{t}^{2}+2t-2\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]{t}^{2}+[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 2\end{aligned}]t+[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2\end{aligned}].
$$

Solving the fourth equation and then substituting the corresponding values ​​into the first and fifth equations to solve for a2 and b2, we get
